newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian police seize fruit-flavored cocaine.
newsitem.headline: Colombian police seize fruit-flavored cocaine.

text.p: Anti-narcotics police in Bogota seized 340 pounds (156 kg) of fruit-flavored cocaine bound for Miami on Saturday, the authorities said.
The drug had been mixed with crushed blackberries and pineapples in order to mask the smell and fool police sniffer dogs.

Police said the cocaine would have been separated from the fruit on arrival in the United States by mixing it with sulphuric acid. Three men and a woman were arrested in the operation, a police spokesman said.

International drug traffickers have used a variety of methods to try and smuggle cocaine into the United States, including mixing it with other materials to make seemingly inoffensive dog kennels, fencing posts and wigs.
U.S. anti-narcotics agents estimate Colombia supplies 80 percent of the world's cocaine.
